\begin{restated}{Remark}{rem:B3-fresh}{B3}{0}{the square-norm step discards the control variate}
Suppose the memory is fresh, $z_i=\fip(\theta)$ for all $i$ (e.g.\ at $t=1$ with the book's initialization, or approximately when the iterates move slowly). Then $\omega_t=\Fp(\theta)$ is deterministic, $\Omega=\norm{\Fp(\theta)}^2$, $M=S$, $B=S/n-\norm{\Fp(\theta)}^2$ and
\[
r_{\mathrm{sq}}=\frac{\norm{\Fp(\theta)}^2}{4S/n-2\norm{\Fp(\theta)}^2}\le\frac12,\qquad\text{with }r_{\mathrm{sq}}\ll\frac12\text{ when }\frac Sn\gg\norm{\Fp(\theta)}^2,
\]
i.e.\ when the per-sample gradient changes $a_i$ are diverse. In general, if index $i$ was last drawn at time $u_i\le t-1$, then $z_i=z^{(u_i)}_i=\fip(\theta_{u_i-1})$ by \eqref{eq:B3-saga}; writing $s_i:=u_i-1\in\{0,\dots,t-2\}$, and $s_i:=0$ for the indices not yet drawn (with the book's initialization $z^{(0)}_i=\fip(\theta_0)$), one has $z_i=\fip(\theta_{s_i})$ in all cases, and
\[
C=\inner{\Fp(\theta)}{\bar z}-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\inner{a_i(\theta)}{a_i(\theta_{s_i})},\qquad a_i(\theta'):=\fip(\theta')-\fip(\etastar):
\]
the correlation between the current gradient change and the stored one is exactly what the control variate $-z_{i(t)}+\bar z$ exploits, and (I1) discards it. Since $\Fp(\theta)=\frac1n\sum_ia_i(\theta)$ and $\bar z=\frac1n\sum_ia_i(\theta_{s_i})$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:B3-consequences}(a)), this is
\[
C=-\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\inner{a_i(\theta)-\Fp(\theta)}{a_i(\theta_{s_i})-\bar z},
\]
minus the empirical covariance over $i$ of the current and the stored gradient changes, whose sign is not determined in general: $r_{\mathrm{sq}}<\frac12$ iff this covariance is positive. Moreover $\abs{r_{\mathrm{sq}}-\frac12}=\abs C/(S/n+B)\le\sqrt x/(1+x)$ with $x:=B/(S/n)$, by Lemma~\ref{lem:B3-identities}(e), so that $r_{\mathrm{sq}}\ll\frac12$ requires both a strong positive correlation and $B$ comparable with $S/n$. One therefore expects two regimes. When the memory is nearly fresh, i.e.\ when the iterates move little during the $\approx n$ iterations that refresh it (for the textbook step, roughly when $2n\gamma\muEff\lesssim1$, which requires $\kappa\gtrsim n/2$), the correlation is strong, $r_{\mathrm{sq}}\le\frac12$ (possibly $\ll\frac12$) and (I1) loses at least a factor $2$ in the $\gamma^2$ terms. When the iterates move fast compared with this refresh, the stored errors dominate ($x\gg1$), the covariance may have either sign, and $r_{\mathrm{sq}}$ stays close to $\frac12$ on either side, since $\sqrt x/(1+x)\le1/\sqrt x$: (I1) still costs a factor close to $2$. The experiments show both regimes (Section~\ref{sec:B3-measure}).
\end{restated}
